- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–3%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or overshoots early; adjust downward by 1–2% for first 5–7 days of forecast horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects or fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag mean reversion; align forecast midpoint with 3–5 day moving average of true prices.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates near end of horizon; cap final 5–7 days at 1–2% below recent true trend.
- If sentiment is neutral or flat (0.00–0.33), model tends to drift upward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for 3–5 days ahead.
